description: Check whether the learner has met each term (a word or phrase in the language being learned). Matching ignores case, accents, punctuation and one leading article from a built-in best-effort list of common articles of several Latin-script European languages (other languages get no article handling). Each result has met, match ('exact', 'in_sentence', 'translation' or 'none'), items (exact matches), in_sentences (longer phrases containing the term) and in_translations (words whose translation contains the term, for terms in the learner's own language); 'translation' means only translations matched. No stemming: if a conjugated or plural form is not found, also try its dictionary form (e.g. the infinitive). Terms shorter than 3 characters, or a lone article, match exactly only. state: 'any' (default) = every word you have met; 'fully_learned_or_known' = only fully learned or already-known words. If some lesson details cannot be fetched, results are still returned without those lesson links and a `warnings` field names the failed lesson ids. Each word row has word (in the language being learned) and translation (its meaning in the learner's own language). next_review is null unless the word is learned (words never studied, or already known, have none). heard is Memrise's own flag that the word has been heard (its trigger is not documented); heard: true on a word that is not learned or known means only heard, never studied. origin is 'lesson' when a completed or in-progress lesson teaches the word, 'other' when none does (words you have only heard, heard: true, not learned or known, from content outside your lessons; next_review is null so they never look overdue), 'unknown' when none is linked but a lesson failed to load (see warnings); words that are not 'lesson' have no lessons or topics. The first call in a fresh process with a cold cache is noticeably slower because every completed lesson is fetched once; later calls are fast.
name: learnables_lookup
title: Look up learner words
